title: otisk klíče serveru ČSOB
interface: final class Drupal\csobrec\Service\HostKeyCheck, no constructor arguments. fingerprint(string $hostKey): string takes a public key in the format phpseclib's SSH2::getServerPublicHostKey() returns — '<type> <base64>' possibly with a trailing comment and surrounding whitespace — and returns the OpenSSH fingerprint 'SHA256:' . rtrim(base64_encode(hash('sha256', <raw key blob>, TRUE)), '='): the exact string `ssh-keygen -lf` prints, so the operator can compare by eye. Anything that is not two whitespace-separated words whose second word is valid base64 is \InvalidArgumentException. verify(string $hostKey, ?string $expected, bool $enforce): string computes the fingerprint and returns it so the caller can log it. When $expected is a non-empty string it must match, otherwise \RuntimeException naming BOTH fingerprints (they are public; that is what tells a key rotation from an attack). $expected is compared tolerantly: surrounding whitespace, a missing 'SHA256:' prefix and base64 '=' padding all still match. When $expected is NULL or empty and $enforce is TRUE, \RuntimeException — 'verify the key' with nothing to verify against must not pass. When $expected is empty and $enforce is FALSE, return the fingerprint. Note the deliberate difference from the Python version: a configured fingerprint is ALWAYS compared, so filling otisk and forgetting overit_klic cannot look verified and verify nothing.
